title: TasksBackend::update_task_per_user default delegates to update_object — multi-user backends that forget to override silently violate draft-tasks-06 §4.5.1 shared-timestamp invariant
description:
crate-jmap-tasks-server/src/backend.rs:106-126:

    fn update_task_per_user(
        &self,
        caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
        account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
        id: &jmap_types::Id,
        patch: PatchObject,
    ) -> impl std::future::Future<
        Output = Result<Option<jmap_tasks_types::Task>, BackendSetError<Self::Error>>,
    > + Send {
        // Task::Patch = PatchObject (see jmap_tasks_types backend.rs).
        self.update_object::<jmap_tasks_types::Task>(caller, account_id, id, patch)
    }

draft-tasks-06 §4.5.1 lines 978-981 are normative: when a patch contains only per-user properties (keywords, color, freeBusyStatus, useDefaultAlerts, alerts), the shared \"updated\" timestamp on the Task object MUST NOT change. The default implementation delegates to update_object, which (per the same trait) updates the shared object — bumping the shared timestamp. This is a spec violation in every multi-user backend that uses the default.

The docstring is half-honest:

    The default implementation delegates to [\`Self::update_object\`], which is correct
    for single-user scenarios but backends serving multiple users SHOULD override this
    method to route to a user-scoped patch path.

Two problems:

  1. \"SHOULD override\" is too weak. The cost of not overriding in a multi-user backend is a spec-violating side effect that the client may not even notice (the timestamp bump is correct for shared mutations and the per-user-only routing is the only case it matters). A consumer who tests against a single-user fixture will never hit this, and only discover the bug when a real second user shows up.

  2. \"Single-user scenarios\" is a slippery framing. A single-user reference backend (MockBackend, MemoryBackend) is permitted to delegate. But the JMAP server kit's reason for existing is multi-user JMAP. Treating multi-user as the special case that requires opt-in is backwards.

Three plausible contract strengthenings:

  - Make the method required (no default). Single-user backends explicitly opt-in to the no-op-delegate pattern by writing the one-liner. Cost: minor boilerplate. Benefit: type system catches the silent-spec-violation case.

  - Add a tracking sibling fn that the handler can use to enforce \"either you implement update_task_per_user properly, or you assert that you're a single-user backend\". E.g. fn is_single_user(&self) -> bool { false } with the default impl delegating only when is_single_user() is true and otherwise returning a runtime error from update_task_per_user's default.

  - Rename the default delegation to update_task_per_user_single_user_only as the default impl, with a doc comment that is unambiguous: \"WARNING: delegates to update_object, which violates draft-tasks-06 §4.5.1 for multi-user backends. Override or assert single-user.\"

The current shape ships in 0.1.x; the contract is locked at the moment a multi-user consumer ships with the default. Workspace test-integrity violation potential is high: no integration test in this crate verifies that update_task_per_user does NOT bump the shared timestamp (only that it is *called* — see lib.rs:786-815 per_user_patch_split test which counts call count, not timestamp effect).

Related: JMAP-h47t.5 (MemoryBackend.query_objects silently ignores sort/filter) is a parallel case of the same anti-pattern — the reference impl teaches consumers an incorrect default. Same architectural defect at the trait-default layer here.

Triage 2026-10-19 at 9fdbbbcf, DUPLICATE (3-skeptic check 3/3 upheld): The defect is still present at HEAD 9fdbbbcf. crate-jmap-tasks-server/src/backend.rs:234-264 still has the default `fn update_task_per_user(...) { self.update_object::<jmap_tasks_types::Task>(caller, account_id, id, patch) }`. Its doc comment still says multi-user backends "SHOULD override", even though the doc itself cites the §4.5.1 MUST NOT for the shared `updated` timestamp.

JMAP-ops7.23 (open, P1, filed 2026-05-17) describes exactly the same defect: "tasks-server: TasksBackend::update_task_per_user default silently violates draft-tasks-06 §4.5.1 in multi-user deployments". It gives the same remedy, dropping the default, which is option (a) in this bead's 2026-05-14 comment. ops7.23 also links the calendars sibling JMAP-ic0j.26 and asks for both to land in one workspace sweep, so it is the better tracking bead.
